firstSentence: Automate adverse drug reaction (ADR) detection and MedDRA coding across clinical trial records, classifying critical safety events in sub-45ms under CDSCO and FDA FAERS mandates.

paragraphs: Pharmaceutical drug sponsors and clinical research organizations (CROs) in India process thousands of adverse event reports, post-marketing spontaneous complaints, and patient registries weekly. Pharmacovigilance safety teams spend weeks manually reading unstructured physician notes, determining drug causality, and mapping reported side effects to the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA). Regulatory delays in reporting Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) within statutory 7-day or 15-day windows trigger clinical trial suspensions and massive regulatory fines.

Our sovereign pharmacovigilance architecture deploys automated safety triage state machines inside air-gapped private VPC enclaves. Unstructured adverse event narratives, physician clinical notes, and patient spontaneous reports are ingested through secure API gateways. The deep learning reasoning engine extracts suspect drugs, concomitant medications, event onset dates, and clinical outcomes with sub-45ms latency.

The pharmacovigilance state machine maps extracted adverse symptoms directly to MedDRA Lower Level Terms (LLT) and Preferred Terms (PT) with 99.4% precision. It applies algorithmic Naranjo and WHO-UMC causality assessment algorithms, evaluating challenge-dechallenge-rechallenge timelines and biological plausibility. Serious adverse events (such as hospitalization, disability, or death) immediately trigger automated E2B(R3) electronic safety XML package generation ready for regulatory submission.

Statutory compliance satisfies Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI) rules, US FDA FAERS 21 CFR 314.80 mandates, and EMA EudraVigilance guidelines. The system cuts adverse event triage turnaround from 14 business days to under 2 hours, eliminating regulatory reporting non-compliance risk.

faqs.question: Does the system differentiate between expected and unexpected adverse drug reactions?
faqs.answer: Yes. The engine cross-references extracted events against the approved Investigator Brochure (IB) or Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS), automatically flagging unexpected events for accelerated reporting.

faqs.question: Can the system process literature abstracts and spontaneous consumer complaints?
faqs.answer: Yes. The pipeline ingests published biomedical literature (PubMed/Europe PMC) and consumer call center transcripts, filtering non-safety noise and extracting valid ICSR cases.

faqs.question: How does the system ensure compliance with statutory 7-day fatal/life-threatening reporting deadlines?
faqs.answer: The state machine flags fatal or life-threatening cases with highest priority, immediately notifying safety physicians via automated escalation channels to ensure regulatory filing within 7 calendar days.
